example: We don't always see eye to eye, but we respect each other's opinions.
origin: Believed to come from the idea of two people looking at something from the same point of view

wrong_meanings.meaning: to look at something very carefully
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This describes looking closely, but the idiom is about having the same opinion, not about eyesight.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to have problems with your eyesight
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom has nothing to do with eyes or eye health; it uses the word 'eye' only as a metaphor.
The idiom describes agreement or disagreement of opinions, not the way people speak during an argument.

explanation: 'See eye to eye' means that two people share the same opinion. It is most often used in negative sentences ('don't see eye to eye') to say that people disagree.
